description: Open-ended skill acquisition, forgetting and expression. Every constant cites docs/research/skill_acquisition_ledger.md (E#) or is [U]. Tags: [V] implemented from supported evidence; [D] direction or ordering only, magnitude a free default; [U] placeholder without usable evidence (covered by devsim.skills.sensitivity_sweep). Times are in days.

transfer_similarity_cutoff.note: below this label similarity transfer is exactly 0 (far transfer null, E24 [V]); the cutoff itself is a placeholder

transfer_gain.note: near-transfer rate boost = 1 + gain x similarity x level of the related skill

aptitude_mode.note: one seeded latent z per agent; the only new agent-level variable (design flag for the owner)

rho_skill.note: cognitive ability with skill acquisition (Colquitt et al. 2000, rho .38); used only to scale the aptitude effect

log_rate_sigma.note: between-person spread of log learning rate; beta_apt = rho_skill x log_rate_sigma (mapping [U], direction [D])

openness_link.note: no verified openness effect on learning rate; off

alpha_shape.note: gamma shape of the per (agent, skill) base rate; the gamma FORM is [V] (E2: averaging gamma-rate exponentials gives a power law)

alpha_mean.note: mean base acquisition rate per full-quality practice

ceiling0.note: first-segment asymptote; strategy shifts raise it (later pieces surpass earlier ones, E4 [C])

s0_mean_days.note: mean initial stability before decay-class scaling

k_s.note: stability gain per practice; gain grows with the gap since the last one (spacing direction E8 [D])

p_gap.note: exponent on (1 - R) in the stability gain

mode_mult_restudy.note: acquisition multiplier for restudy (testing effect: retrieval at least as good)

mode_s_retrieval.note: stability gain multiplier for retrieval (g about 0.5 direction, magnitude free)

feedback_self.note: self-focused feedback does not help and may hurt slightly

savings_gain.note: relearning after a long gap is faster with more prior practice (magnitude [U])

savings_n.note: practices at which savings are about two thirds saturated

decay_cognitive.note: stability scale exp(-c x attribute); ordering cognitive faster than physical [D]; ln 1.55 used only as a plausibility range

decay_accuracy.note: accuracy-graded decays faster than speed-graded [D]; ln 3 used only as a plausibility range

strategy_shift.note: abrupt strategy shifts with a temporary dip (mechanism E4 [C]; parameters [U])

h_shift.note: shift hazard per full-quality practice, shrinking as level approaches the ceiling

dip.note: temporary drop in level at a shift

shift_boost.note: rate multiplier for the new segment

shift_ceiling_gain.note: share of the remaining headroom the new segment adds to the ceiling

w_sleep.note: performance loss from sleep pressure above sleep_ref (direction E19/E20 [D]; magnitude unknown)

sleep_ref.note: sleep pressure below which performance is unaffected

w_stress.note: performance loss from stress above stress_ref; no inverted U, no choking term (NOT FOUND)

stress_ref.note: stress readout below which performance is unaffected

tier_novice.note: performance at or above this is a beginner (below: none)

competence_noise.note: seeded noise on a competence check

r_self.note: target correlation of perceived with true skill in the reference population; noise is calibrated to it; no built-in overconfidence (E23 contested)

familiar_noise_cut.note: share of self-assessment noise removed for a well-practised skill (direction E22 [D])

clarity_noise_cut.note: share removed with objective, immediate feedback (direction E22 [D])

conscientiousness_motivation.note: conscientiousness raises wanting to practise (motivation .38), never the learning rate

anxiety_motivation.note: anxiety lowers wanting to practise (motivation -.57); neuroticism and threat sensitivity as anxiety is a [U] mapping

anxiety_attention.note: mild attention reduction during practice (outcomes -.15 direction)

practice_menu_weight.note: how much practice wanting adds to a living-world activity option

eps_level.note: prune to a savings record below this level

max_skills_per_agent.note: safety valve: least important skills become savings records

event_log_cap.note: practice events kept per skill for audit and replay

tier_text.none: You have never learned this. You do not know how it works: you may be confused, guess tentatively, ask for help, change the subject, or say honestly that you do not know. Never invent a confident answer.
tier_text.novice: You are a beginner at this: you know a few basics, are unsure, make hesitant attempts and readily ask for help.
tier_text.competent: You can do this reasonably well, with some effort and the occasional slip.
tier_text.proficient: You are good at this and can do it with confidence.
tier_text.expert: You are an expert at this and can do it fluently, even explaining it to others.
